_comment: ADVISORY committed baseline for the didChange round-trip benchmark. A REFERENCE point captured on an Apple M-series / macOS dev machine, --release. Criterion's live target/criterion/ baseline is gitignored and runner-local; the 20%-regression comparison is reliable only on a pinned/self-hosted runner. On shared CI the benchmark is informational. The HARD gate is tests/didchange_budget.rs (margined wall-clock).
_rebaselined: 2026-08-13, and the reason is not drift. The fixture was rewritten into the surface of grammar.bnf (no `prefix`, bare property keys, `@subject`, `str.*` after ruling 16) and it now NAMES a shape document, which the old one could not. More importantly the HOST changed: both this benchmark and the hard gate built their db on `fossil_base::NativeSystem`, whose provider table reads no types — so the shape document never decoded, `resolve_target_shape` failed for all 15 mappings, and what was being measured was the error path. Both now install `fossil_descriptors_output::PROVIDERS` and register the document, as `fossil-lsp`'s own `LspSystem` does. The old 120042 ns is not comparable to the new figure in either direction and is kept below only so nobody re-derives a regression from it.
measures: set_text (Salsa Setter, revision bump) -> def_map -> typecheck_mapping over every mapping (each resolving its target shape against the registered document) -> drain Diagnostic accumulator

measuring_the_real_path_is_not_slower._comment: Same machine, same fixture, same loop, only the host differs — 10 measured iterations after 2 warm-ups, --release. Resolving the contract COSTS NOTHING NET: the decode is memoised and keyed by the document's SourceFile, so editing the program re-runs it zero times, while the failing path was pushing 32 diagnostics through the accumulator on every keystroke.

superseded.why_not_comparable: different program, and a host that resolved no output contract
